native_compile.how: Build via README Quick start; read info_material and info_material_back.

native_backface_pass.how: Turn on Inputs > Back-face pass; run study_tools inspect(component)['backface']; render_back's Render toggle follows the switch (lenient expression); no Geometry COMP references a material any more (Override Material), so no reference cycle is expected; compare Exit normal stage with and without the pass.

native_flip_v.how: Confirm the refraction is upright with Flip screen V off. Then the orientation check: back-face pass on, Stage Thickness, a Sphere SOP at IOR 1.5: the profile must be symmetric top to bottom as well as left to right, and a slab rotated about the camera's horizontal axis must shift the view the same way as in the preview. The shader measures the screen orientation per pixel by comparing the projected position with gl_FragCoord; this confirms it in the real build. Also (verifier round): with Reflection map = Flat image TOP, tilt the camera up and down; the flat-image reflection must slide the same way as the bends do. Render once at an odd resolution (for example 1281 x 721): no one-pixel seam across the glass on the centre row or column. The shader also multiplies the flat-image offset by the projection matrix's own sign; a build whose uTDMats proj has a negative y scale is the case this guards.

controls.how: component.op('study_tools').module.apply(component, id) for each experiment in experiments.json, in any order; confirm the setup controls (Inputs, Object size, Reflection map, Demo render) survive.

preset_callback.how: Change Glass > Preset and confirm the sliders change.

native_material_path.how: Drag the component's material onto a Geometry COMP outside the component, and separately type the path the build printed. Both must render the glass. Record the relative form TouchDesigner shows (independent review T3).

native_backface_several_objects.how: Type two glass objects into Inputs > Glass geometry, separated by a space; render_back must render both and backface_report(component)['glass_objects'] must list both. If the field takes only one object, use render_back's Geometry parameter and note the build (T4).

native_backface_negative_alpha.how: With the pass on, backface_report(component, sample=True)['glass_texels'] must be above 0 (negative alpha survives the 32-bit float Render TOP with Pre-Multiply off). Give the camera a background colour with alpha 0.5: the Thickness stage must not change (T5).

native_no_normals.how: A SOP without a normal attribute (for example a Box SOP followed by an Attribute SOP that deletes N) as glass: record what TDNormal() returns (Normal stage); the glass must show faceted normals in both passes (T6).

native_picking.how: A Render Pick DAT on the demo render: picking the torus must return demo_geo, and info_material must stay free of errors while picking is active (T8). Family close G6: the pick render now runs only the placement and TDWritePickingValues() and writes none of the four outputs; if picks over the glass come back wrong while ordinary renders look right, the build reads more than the documented #else block.

native_colour_space.how: Record the project's working colour space with every native capture. Presets were tuned in Pass Through; under ACEScg render_back becomes 16-bit float (T5).

native_render_pass_route.how: A scene Render TOP without the glass, a box between camera and glass, then a Render Pass TOP on it (Clear Depth Buffer and Clear to Camera Color off, Override Material = material): the box must stay in front of the glass, and TouchDesigner must not report a problem with the material sampling the render the pass builds on (family sync R2).

native_inputs_constant_mode.how: After the build, the Inputs fields show relative paths in constant mode; drag a TOP on, clear it, Reset to Default; no 'inputs' build warning (R3).

native_dither_default.how: Record the Render TOP's default Dither in the installed build; render and render_back must show Dither off, or a 'dither' build warning (C4).

native_drift_clock.how: With Wobble on, animate Morph between two presets with different Wobble speeds after the project has run for a while: the ripples must not jump; absTime appears in no node expression (R1).

native_colour_buffers_and_fog.how: A Render TOP with # of Color Buffers 3 drawing the glass: no errors, buffers 1 and 2 unchanged; Camera COMP fog on: the glass fades into the fog like the scene (C2, C7).

native_fit_glass.how: Pulse Inputs > Fit to Glass geometry on the demo: Object size stays 0.872517 (the family close's default; it was 1 before). On a Sphere SOP of radius 0.1 and 10: 0.0689655 and 6.89655 (radius over 1.45). On the demo torus with its Geometry COMP scaled 3 (sx, sy, sz 3, 3, 1.8): 2.61755, and the ripples (Lavender Prism, Teaching stage Normal) and film bands (Prism Chrome, Film) look as on the unscaled demo at 0.872517. SOP.bounds, geometryCOMP.bounds and worldTransform.determinant must exist (C8, family close G1).

native_render_diagnostics.how: inspect(component)['render_diagnostics'] lists the component's renders and a user Render Pass TOP whose Override Material is the material; script_errors is a string (C5, R9).

native_oit_discard.how: Render Transparency = Order Independent Transparency, Opacity 0.5, Spectral Prism on the demo knot (self-overlapping), with and without the back-face pass: no errors in info_render, no blocky or noisy rims compared with Transparency off (footprintLod's derivatives run before TDCheckDiscard()). checks.how: Build the component: Object size reads 0.872517. Scale demo_geo by 3 (keeping its flattened depth) and press Fit to Glass geometry: Object size reads 2.61755, and the ripples and film bands look as on the unscaled demo, seen from 3 times as far.

Set the demo render to 481 x 271 (odd both ways). With Flip screen V off, look at Stage screenuv and the bent checker: no one-pixel seam on the centre row or column. Note whether your build's raster runs down or up (whether the refraction needs Flip screen V).
In a scene of your own, follow the README's Render Pass TOP route with an opaque object in front of the glass: it stays in front, as in the preview's render_pass_keeps_foreground_in_front.

Point a Render Pick DAT at the demo render and pick over the glass: it should report the demo Geometry COMP with positions and normals on its surface, and info_material and info_render show no error for the pick variant (only the '#else' block runs: TDWritePickingValues()).

Family open question (centre-line residual). Set the demo render to 481 x 271 (odd both ways) with Anti-Alias at 4x and Flip screen V off, as in odd_size_481x271. Copy the render, the material and its pixel shader DAT. In the copied DAT, replace `cam.screenSign = screenSign(ndc, ndcStep, depthStep);` with `cam.screenSign = vec2(1.0, 1.0);`: the orientation every other glass pixel measures in TouchDesigner's usual raster (use -1.0 for y if odd_size_481x271 found that the raster runs up). Point the copied material's pixel shader at the copied DAT and the copied render's Override Material at the copied material. With Pause on, wire both renders into a Composite TOP with Operation Difference. An Analyze TOP with Operation Maximum in RGB gives the largest difference; the pixels that are not black are where the orientation was wrong. Repeat at several Fixed times so silhouettes cross the centre row and column. Record the build, the GPU, how many pixels differ, the largest difference, and whether those pixels show at 100% zoom in the delivered image. The preview's numbers for this study are under preview.
checks.if_visible: If any of them is visible, try a centroid-qualified vertex output for the projected position in Liquid Glass Lit first (Lit's form (e): a second vertex output, `centroid out vec3 vOrientPos`, holding the world position and read only for the projected position in screenSign()). In Lit's preview survey it fixed the usual raster (17 residual pixels to 1) but not the flipped one (18 to 16). Measure it with Lit's survey and this check, then bring it to the core, to Flow with the core's pixel stage, and to Prism. If none is visible, close the open question with this record.

centre_line_residual.scope: Family critic (low): a few multisampled silhouette pixels near a centre line take the wrong orientation sign. Measured here: screen_orientation_has_no_wrong_pixels: 8 wrong multisampled pixels in 144 renders, at most 2 per row of twelve (3 in the normal raster), and 1 wrong single-sample pixel. Final image (checks/results/centre-line-residual.json; each render drawn as delivered and with the orientation set to the right value, 4x multisampled canvas): 24 pixels change in 144 renders, at most 7 per row, 7 by more than 8/255, the largest by 20/255 (Diamond Fire on the knot, normal raster, 480 x 270); in the normal raster, TouchDesigner's usual orientation, 13 pixels, by up to 20/255. 23 of them lie within 4 pixels of a centre line; the last, 5 pixels from the centre column, changes by 1/255. More pixels change than take the wrong sign, probably because the footprint level reads screen derivatives of the bent lookups, which a wrong neighbour in the same 2 x 2 block changes (an inference, not measured). Kept as a family open question (co-design.json) with the native check centre_line_residual (family_close.native_run); no shader changed. screen_orientation_has_no_wrong_pixels now allows at most 10 wrong multisampled pixels per row (20 before). Unit tests CentreLineResidual (2) fail on the files before this round.
